title: Trump DOJ Election Fraud Crackdown Nets More Than 200 Arrests, Indictments
text:
The Trump administration’s nationwide election enforcement push has resulted in more than 200 arrests and indictments involving alleged election fraud and noncitizen voting , with a senior Justice Department official saying additional cases are coming.
Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon said the Justice Department has indicted or convicted 67 people for election-related crimes in recent weeks, while the Department of Homeland Security has made more than 160 arrests.
“I think there are a lot of nervous election officials because I think some of them know that they’ve been looking the other way when this is happening, and we’re catching it all over the country,” Dhillon told Just the News.
Dhillon also questioned New Jersey’s explanation that a computer glitch allowed thousands of noncitizens to register and roughly 400 to vote, saying federal officials are investigating the matter.
The enforcement effort comes as the Justice Department has announced a series of election-related prosecutions. On Sept. 18, DOJ charged 16 people with offenses involving illegal voting, voter registration and related alleged election fraud. The cases included noncitizens accused of voting in federal elections and falsely claiming U.S. citizenship.
Other recent cases include charges against individuals in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Wisconsin, California, Kansas and Louisiana. DOJ also charged three people in a Los Angeles scheme involving allegedly paying people to sign ballot petitions using stolen identities of registered voters.
Dhillon said the administration intends to continue expanding its enforcement efforts.
“What we care about is that noncitizens who voted in a federal election canceled out the votes of American citizens,” she said.
